newsitem.title: ITALY: Fx rates touchy topic at Italy/France summit - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Fx rates touchy topic at Italy/France summit - Dini.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Wednesday he expected foreign exchange rates to be the touchy topic of an Italo-French summit this week.
Shortly before Dini spoke to reporters at parliament, the lira hit a two-year high against the German mark.
"I think we will have a splendid meeting," Dini said. "There are no great differences between us and the French. There are, however, great sensitivities over exchange rates.
"The lira is already very strong," he added.
The Italian currency earlier touched a high of 994.00 against the mark, equalling a previous level reached on August 4, 1994, dealers said.

Italy and France have been trying to paper over a diplomatic row on Tuesday caused by a suggestion by French President Jacques Chirac that Italy might not be in shape to join a planned European economic and monetary union at its launch in 1999.
Italy almost scrapped Thursday and Friday's summit but hasty back-pedalling by Chirac ensured the meeting would go ahead.
